dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: Pm-3m five-site perovskite hydride: Mg 1a, Ir 1b, H on the three face-center sites (origin/basis equivalent to ABH3)
candidate.prototype_evidence: Pm-3m five-site perovskite hydride: Mg 1a, Ir 1b, H on the three face-center sites (origin/basis equivalent to ABH3)
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: Hydrogen stoichiometry, anharmonicity and competing complex hydrides are the important physical risks. Hansen et al. observed a minor Pm-3m MgIrHx phase but could not establish x, potentially even zero; their Mg2IrH5 synthesis and proposed Mg2IrH6 superconductivity are different stoichiometries/prototypes. These priors neither establish MgIrH3 superconductivity nor invalidate the exact locally stable model. Neglected Ir SOC and different PP/cutoff between Rh and Ir remain matched-method falsifiers.
candidate.ambient_scope: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.108 GPa, full max stress=0.108 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
candidate.route_response: Ir replaces Rh on the single transition-metal site while the Mg and three H roles remain mapped. The volume rises 3.573%, with the actual H-metal and H-H distances retained below. Lambda improves at all ten sigma values, whereas the separate Eli mu=.1 change is modest, 11.198 to 11.862 K; this distinction avoids ranking solely by coupling.
candidate.next_action: At the same ordered MgIrH3/MgRhH3 geometry roles, separate common-volume chemical substitution from expansion and test H stoichiometry/anharmonic modes. A persistent direct coupling advantage without an unstable H/order branch supports screening; a stable hydrogen-deficient insulating phase or erased coupling advantage opposes it.

seven_criteria.identity: Complete ordered CIF/literal coarse-fine input/Gamma periodic species-site association is numerically supported; source input geometry and full tensor/forces are retained. Export occupancy is a discrete computational convention; source experimental P/T/occupancy and actual compiled unit constant are unknown. Exact-version input defaults scope the configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC model, not magnetic ground state.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Ir replaces Rh on the single transition-metal site while the Mg and three H roles remain mapped. The volume rises 3.573%, with the actual H-metal and H-H distances retained below. Lambda improves at all ten sigma values, whereas the separate Eli mu=.1 change is modest, 11.198 to 11.862 K; this distinction avoids ranking solely by coupling.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Exact target and mapped control direct source lambda arrays have the same favorable sign at all ten common broadening tokens; omega_ln has explicit K units and separate Eli/McM mu=.1 tables remain independent. Same underlying q mesh is observed. The sensitivity range is not a physical error bound; sigma units, full-BZ convergence, experimental Tc and pure-geometry causality remain unknown. Literal method differences are declared confounds.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.108 GPa, full max stress=0.108 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: Hydrogen stoichiometry, anharmonicity and competing complex hydrides are the important physical risks. Hansen et al. observed a minor Pm-3m MgIrHx phase but could not establish x, potentially even zero; their Mg2IrH5 synthesis and proposed Mg2IrH6 superconductivity are different stoichiometries/prototypes. These priors neither establish MgIrH3 superconductivity nor invalidate the exact locally stable model. Neglected Ir SOC and different PP/cutoff between Rh and Ir remain matched-method falsifiers.
seven_criteria.novelty: The 2026-10-07 bounded MgIrH3/IrMgH3 search found a related experimentally observed Pm-3m MgIrHx phase with unknown hydrogen content, not an exact experimental superconducting MgIrH3 benchmark. The new-to-reviewed-catalogue object is the fully ordered H3 occupancy and matched Ir-for-Rh hypothesis; no first-composition claim.
seven_criteria.decision: At the same ordered MgIrH3/MgRhH3 geometry roles, separate common-volume chemical substitution from expansion and test H stoichiometry/anharmonic modes. A persistent direct coupling advantage without an unstable H/order branch supports screening; a stable hydrogen-deficient insulating phase or erased coupling advantage opposes it.
